instruction: COMPLETENESS/GOVERNANCE-lens R1 review of WP-SCP-022 slice 020L (first rule-RFC dogfood) at branch feature/wp-scp-022-020l-rule-rfc-dogfood. Closes post-Threshold-A backlog item 'WP-SCP-022 proposal-queue'. Slice surface: docs/reviews/rule-proposals/RULE-001-waiver-reason-must-cite-issue-or-pr.md (NEW, ~270 lines) + docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/020l/DISPATCH-NOTE.md (NEW). This slice is the FIRST exercise of the rule-RFC process landed at slice 020H.1 (`docs/reviews/rule-proposals/README.md` + `RULE-TEMPLATE.md`); a PRIMARY review goal is to find process gaps that would block any subsequent RFC. Verify COMPLETENESS and GOVERNANCE: (1) Template adherence. RULE-TEMPLATE.md prescribes §1-§11 with specific subsections (§3.1-§3.4, §4 with FP enumeration, §5 with implicit-exclusion set, etc.). Read RULE-TEMPLATE.md and verify RULE-001 covers every required section + subsection. Flag any missing or under-specified section. (2) Front-matter completeness. Per RULE-TEMPLATE.md lines 1-10, front-matter has: Status, Author, Filed, Target release, Type, Quorum required, Review window, Bypass-surface non-empty. Verify all 8 fields are present + correctly populated. (3) §1 Summary self-containment. RULE-TEMPLATE.md §1 says 'adopter who reads only this paragraph should be able to decide whether they want to engage'. Verify §1 names rule ID, match-condition one-liner, severity, target release. (4) §2 Motivation cites a real-world finding. RULE-TEMPLATE.md §2 + README.md §Authorship guidance both require this. The proposal cites 'audit-trail gap structural rather than single incident' — judge whether this is concrete enough or whether reviewers should request a more specific finding citation. (5) §3 Rule specification: §3.1 (match), §3.2 (severity), §3.3 (annotation), §3.4 (sketch) all present + filled. (6) §4 False-positive surface enumerates ≥2 named cases with rate estimate + recommended response. Verify FP-1 / FP-2 / FP-3 are concrete + actionable. (7) §5 Bypass surface: explicit enumeration even for `None`. The implicit-exclusion set is named per 020H.1 R1 SAFE-MAJ-002 closure. Verify the 4 cases are exhaustive. (8) §6 Conflict-gate strategy: §6.1 Python parity expressible? §6.2 fixture corpus enumerated? §6.3 disagreement risk assessed? (9) §7 Estate-cascade considerations: all 6 named adopters classified per WP-SCP-024 plan. Verify the proposal's per-adopter assessment is consistent with MEMORY entries (project_estate_structure.md, project_auth_conformance_state.md, reference_fla_gold_standard.md, reference_ct_notifications.md). (10) §8 Test plan: Conftest tests + conflict-gate fixtures + workflow-selftest + canary considerations all addressed. (11) §9 Migration / rollout: maps onto VERSIONING.md categories; target release explicit; adopter-side migration steps named. (12) §10 Open questions: every question marked `[BLOCKING]` or `[deferrable]`; pre-resolution for [BLOCKING] questions plus reviewer-confirm hook is per RULE-TEMPLATE.md §10 + 020H.1 R1 SAFE-nit-008 closure. (13) §11 References: cites README.md, RULE-TEMPLATE.md, VERSIONING.md, schemas, ADOPT-001 sections, related rules, related decisions. (14) Process gaps in the RFC infrastructure that this dogfood surfaces. Examples to look for: (a) RULE-TEMPLATE.md prescribes a section the proposal had to invent verbiage for because the template was vague; (b) README.md §Process step doesn't address what to do when the proposal author IS the CODEOWNER (single-operator mode); (c) the 'scp-rule-proposal Renovate label' mentioned at README.md §3 — does this label exist in the repo's labels? (d) the 'auto-defer label' mentioned at README.md §3 — is the label provisioned? (e) PR-template support for proposal PRs vs regular PRs? (f) any other gap exposed by trying to actually walk the process. Flag each gap as a TF-020L-NNN candidate with a closure path. (15) DISPATCH-NOTE.md acceptance criteria (i)-(xvii): each criterion is concrete + verifiable; identifiers match proposal sections; the criterion list is exhaustive (no slice deliverable missed). (16) STATUS.md will need a 'Today's chain (2026-05-02)' row and the Post-Threshold-A backlog 'WP-SCP-022 proposal-queue' line will need amending. Flag this as criterion (xvii) verification — has the proposal-queue line been amended? (Likely no — flag for inclusion in final commit.) (17) Naming convention: 'slice 020L' / 'RFC-001' / 'SCP-R-004' — verify all three are correct + non-colliding (no existing 020L slice; no existing RULE-001.md; no existing SCP-R-004 rule). (18) Future-rule numbering implication: filing this as RFC-001 / SCP-R-004 establishes that RULE-NNN.md numbering and SCP-R-NNN numbering are decoupled (RULE-001 → SCP-R-004 because R-001/002/003 already exist). Flag if README.md should document this convention. NEVER recommend descoping. Findings as JSON with severity, location, description, recommendation.
